info.title: Hourly API
info.description:
A marketplace for freelance work with transparent time tracking. Hierarchy: project -> task -> work session, addressed as `/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/sessions/{sessionId}`. A child requested under a parent it does not belong to answers 404. A known address used with an unsupported method answers 405 with an `Allow` header.

**Hypermedia.** Every resource carries `_links`: related resources (`self`, `project`, `tasks`) and the actions the caller may take right now, with their method (`update`, `publish`, `stop`, `accept`...). Actions follow the role of the caller and the state of the resource. Lists add `first`, `prev`, `next` and `last`. Start at `GET /`.

**Authentication.** `POST /auth/login` returns a short-lived access token (JWT) and sets the `hourly_refresh` cookie. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (the **Authorize** button). When it expires (401 `TOKEN_EXPIRED`), `POST /auth/refresh` issues a new one. After logout, a detected token replay or a password change on another device the token is refused with 401 `SESSION_REVOKED` - sign in again.

get.summary: Entry point: links to everything the caller can reach
get.description: A client that knows only this address can discover the others by following `_links`. What is offered depends on the caller: a guest gets the marketplace and the way in, a signed-in user their own collections, the administrator the user list as well.

_links.description: Hypermedia controls: related resources and the actions the caller may take now

get.summary: Readiness probe: the service and its database
get.description: Answers 503 when the database cannot be reached, so a load balancer or a deployment slot swap can wait for it.

post.summary: Register, choosing the client or specialist role
post.description: The administrator role cannot be chosen. The new user is signed in at once: the response carries the access token and sets the `hourly_refresh` cookie.

409.description: An account with this e-mail already exists (EMAIL_TAKEN)

429.description: Too many attempts (TOO_MANY_REQUESTS); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

post.description: An unknown e-mail and a wrong password get the same 401. A blocked account gets 403 only after its password has been verified. Ten failed attempts for one e-mail from one address within 15 minutes are answered 429 until the window passes; successful sign-ins are not counted.

429.description: Too many attempts (TOO_MANY_REQUESTS); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

post.description: The refresh token is read from the `hourly_refresh` cookie only. Every refresh revokes the presented token and sets a new one, so each token works once. Presenting an already used token revokes every token of that login (REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED).

401.description: Missing, unknown or expired token (INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN), or a reused one (REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED)

429.description: Too many attempts (TOO_MANY_REQUESTS); retry after `Retry-After` seconds

post.description: Ends this login: revokes every refresh token of it and clears the cookie. The access tokens of the login stop working at once too - they name it in their `sid` claim, so the next request with one answers 401 SESSION_REVOKED. Works without an access token and without a cookie (idempotent).

get.description: `scope=marketplace` - publicly published (no token needed), `scope=owned` - created by the user, `scope=assigned` - carried out by the user, `scope=all` - every project, for the administrator only (403 otherwise).

post.description: MARKETPLACE: the actor becomes the client and the project starts as DRAFT. DIRECT: the actor becomes the specialist, `externalClientName` is required and the project starts as IN_PROGRESS. A MARKETPLACE project is created by a client, a DIRECT one by a specialist; any other role gets 403.

_links.description: Hypermedia controls: related resources and the actions the caller may take now

get.description: A PUBLISHED project is public. Any other is visible only to its client, its specialist and the administrator - for everyone else it answers 404.

patch.description: Only the fields present in the body are written. Status changes follow the project lifecycle; PUBLISHED -> IN_PROGRESS happens by accepting a proposal.

_links.description: Hypermedia controls: related resources and the actions the caller may take now

delete.description: Tasks, work sessions, proposals and share links are removed with it. Allowed to the creator of the project (the client of a MARKETPLACE project, the specialist of a DIRECT one) and to the administrator.

get.summary: Project report by task and accumulated hours
get.description: One resource in two representations, selected with the `Accept` header: `application/json` (the default) or `text/csv`, which is returned as a download. Anything else answers 406. Only finished work sessions are counted - a running session has no duration yet. Readable by the parties of the project and the administrator.

406.description: The requested media type is not available

get.description: A personal view, not a second address: tasks of the projects the actor takes part in; `projectId` narrows it to one, `status` and `q` (title and description) filter it. Each task lives at `/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}`.

get.description: A missing project answers 404, which is not the same as an empty list. The tasks are as visible as their project. `status` and `q` (title and description) filter the list.

post.summary: Create a task in the project
post.description: Written by whoever the project named in `taskAuthoring`. Omitting `position` appends the task to the end of the list. The `Location` header points at the new task.

patch.description: Both parties of the project may edit and reorder tasks. `approved` is the decision of the client and applies only when the specialist authored the list.

get.description: A personal view, not a second address: the sessions of the actor. `projectId` and `taskId` narrow it, `from`/`to` select by start time (`from <= startedAt < to`), `running=true` finds the timer still going. `projectId` and `taskId` of each entry give its address under `/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/sessions`.

get.summary: Work sessions of a task (project -> task -> sessions)
get.description: The whole hierarchy in one address. A missing project, or a task that does not belong to it, answers 404 - not an empty list. Logged hours are readable by the parties of the project and the administrator. `from`/`to` select by start time (`from <= startedAt < to`), `running` by whether the timer is going.

post.summary: Start a work session or enter one manually
post.description: Without `endedAt` the session is treated as running. A user may have only one unfinished session at a time, so a second one answers 409. `durationMinutes` and `appliedRate` are computed by the server and cannot be sent in.

get.description: Visible to the client of the project, the administrator and the specialist who submitted it - to the author also after the project went to someone else. For anyone else it answers 404, as it is absent from their list.

patch.summary: Accept, reject or withdraw a proposal
patch.description: ACCEPTED and REJECTED are decisions of the client, WITHDRAWN belongs to the specialist, and only a PENDING proposal can be changed. Accepting runs in one transaction: the offer wins, the competing offers are rejected, and the project moves to IN_PROGRESS with the specialist assigned. Only one proposal per project may be accepted.

post.description: The token is readable only in this response: the database keeps nothing but its SHA-256 hash, so a lost link cannot be recovered, only replaced.

delete.description: The record is kept and stamped with `revokedAt`, because the fact that a project was shared is part of its history. Revoking twice answers 204 again.

get.summary: Project progress behind a share link
get.description: Accessible without an account, read-only. A link that does not exist, one that was revoked and one that expired all answer an identical 404, so a visitor cannot probe which tokens once existed. The response carries an `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header because the token travels in the address.

404.description: Link is invalid, revoked or not found

get.description: Includes the e-mail and the blocked flag. `q` searches the name and the e-mail; `role` and `isBlocked` narrow the list.

delete.description: An account that takes part in projects or has logged work answers 409 (USER_HAS_WORK_HISTORY) - deleting it would erase records of the other party, so it should be blocked instead.
